newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House passes $85 billion net tax cut bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House passes $85 billion net tax cut bill.

text.p: The House of Representatives Thursday approved legislation to cut taxes by a net $85 billion over five years.

The House voted in favour of the bill to implement the tax portion of the balanced budget agreement reached by congressional leaders and President Clinton last month. The Senate was debating its version of tax legislation and was expected to follow suit when it votes.

The House voted 253 to 179 to pass the tax bill. Differences between the House and Senate legislation must be resolved before one final bill is sent to the President. The administration said it "strongly opposes" the House tax bill.
The single biggest piece of the tax cut was a $500-per-child tax credit. The bill also included tax initiatives for college education and expanded Individual Retirement Accounts.
The House legislation would cut the capital gains tax rate to 20 percent from the maximum 28 percent for individuals and gradually reduce the rate for corporations to 30 percent from 35 percent.

The threshold at which the estate tax is imposed would gradually rise to $1 million in 2007 from the current $600,000. The bill would eliminate the ethanol subsidy after it expires at the end of 2000 and raise revenues from airline ticket taxes and passenger fees.
